title: Error Conversion Erasing Needed Classification or Provenance
pattern: A rich, typed error is immediately flattened into text (`.to_string()`, `format!("{:?}", e)`, `.map_err(ToString::to_string)`), or errors from distinct workflow stages (database, HTTP, validation) are collapsed into a common flat representation that discards the type, stage, or cause information callers need to distinguish failures.
why_bad: Callers cannot reliably distinguish validation failures, I/O errors, or transient remote failures, so they either parse messages or apply the wrong recovery (retrying a permanent validation error, rejecting a transient timeout). Lost source chains also obscure which operation in the pipeline actually failed.
detection: Subcase A: inspect `map_err` closures that call `to_string()`, `format!`, or other string conversions where the containing function returns `Result<_, String>`. Subcase B: trace multi-step `?` pipelines and generic error conversions where all subsystem errors are cast to `String` or a flat type-erased container without keeping variant identifiers or source information. In both cases determine whether callers need programmatic distinctions; type erasure alone is not proof that usable provenance was lost.
source: *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 204, Section 14.1); *Rust for Rustaceans* by Jon Gjengset (p. 137); *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 262-263); *Rust for Rustaceans* by Jon Gjengset (p. 137-138).
